messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: merging/moving validate functions
parts:
On 2/23/12 6:23 PM, Daniel Lee wrote:
> Something that's been bothering me is the coupling of
> stan/math/matrix_error_handling.hpp -> stan/prob/transform.hpp. I
> think it should go the other way. I've already started down this road
> of fixing it and it's not too bad. So here are my questions:
> 1) Do you mind that the validate functions are in
> matrix_error_handling? (or just error_handling for non-matrix calls?)
> 2) Should we expose simple validate functions to each of our checks
> within stan/math/*error_handling? return type bool, input only
> accepting the thing we are checking? If not, we can use the full blown
> checks. In fact, I think reader uses the validate function to throw an
> exception, so maybe all we need to do is to call the full method and
> have it use the default policy and throw?
> 3) If we had validate functions, should that be convenience functions
> in namespace stan::prob (where transform lives) or stan::math (where
> the checks live)?
>
> What I would suggest is: 1) move the checks to stan::math. 2) remove
> _validate functions. 3) If we have _validate functions, put them in
> stan::math.
>
> Thoughts? By the way, this would take no effort on your part.

1) Definitely move the checks. And separate them into
matrix_error_handling and error_handling as appropriate.
A dependency of matrix_error_handling on error_handling is OK.

2) That'd be great if you could get rid of the validates and
roll them into error handling. No reason to have two functions.
BUT, there are dependencies from the generated code in:

a. tests for data validity in the constructor
b. tests for transformed data validity in the constructor
c. tests for transformed parameters in write_csv
d. tests for generated quantities in write_csv

There's no validation on the parameters themselves because
they're unbounded and transformed using the various xxx_constrain()
methods in stan::io::reader.

There's also no validation on the inits because that's done
in the various xxx_unconstrain methods in stan::io::writer.

It might be easier if we do this together tomorrow.

3) n/a. See answer to 2.

- Bob

PS: Here's an example of generated validate statements
from a trivial model with every possible variety of
constrained variable.

-------------------------------
data {
real(0,) x;
}
transformed data {
real(0,1) y;
}
parameters {
real(0,) sigma;
}
transformed parameters {
real(0,) sigma_sq;
}
model {
real z;
}
generated quantities {
real(0,1) w;
}
------------------------------


// Code generated by Stan version alpha.0

#include <stan/model/model_header.hpp>

namespace demo_model_namespace {

using std::vector;
using std::string;
using std::stringstream;
using stan::agrad::var;
using stan::model::prob_grad_ad;
using stan::math::get_base1;
using stan::io::dump;
using std::istream;
using namespace stan::math;
using namespace stan::prob;

typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,Eigen::Dynamic,1> vector_d;
typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,1,Eigen::Dynamic> row_vector_d;
typedef Eigen::Matrix<double,Eigen::Dynamic,Eigen::Dynamic> matrix_d;
typedef Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var,Eigen::Dynamic,1> vector_v;
typedef Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var,1,Eigen::Dynamic> row_vector_v;
typedef Eigen::Matrix<stan::agrad::var,Eigen::Dynamic,Eigen::Dynamic>
matrix_v;

class demo_model : public prob_grad_ad {
private:
double x;
double y;
public:
demo_model(stan::io::var_context& context__)
: prob_grad_ad::prob_grad_ad(0) {
size_t pos__;
std::vector<int> vals_i__;
std::vector<double> vals_r__;
x = double(0);
if(!context__.contains_r("x"))
throw std::runtime_error("variable x not found.");
vals_r__ = context__.vals_r("x");
pos__ = 0;
x = vals_r__[pos__++];
// validate data
assert(stan::prob::lb_validate(x,0));
y = double(0);

// validate transformed data
assert(stan::prob::lb_validate(y,0));
assert(stan::prob::ub_validate(y, 1));

set_param_ranges();
} // dump ctor

void set_param_ranges() {
num_params_r__ = 0U;
param_ranges_i__.clear();
++num_params_r__;
}

void transform_inits(const stan::io::var_context& var_context__,
std::vector<int>& params_i__,
std::vector<double>& params_r__) {
params_r__.clear();
params_i__.clear();
stan::io::writer<double> writer__(params_r__,params_i__);
size_t pos__;
std::vector<double> vals_r__;
std::vector<int> vals_i__;


if (!(var_context__.contains_r("sigma")))
throw std::runtime_error("variable sigma missing");
if (var_context__.dims_r("sigma").size() != 0)
throw std::runtime_error("require 0 dimensions for variable
sigma");
vals_r__ = var_context__.vals_r("sigma");
pos__ = 0U;
double sigma(0);
sigma = vals_r__[pos__++];
writer__.scalar_lb_unconstrain(0,sigma);
}

var log_prob(vector<var>& params_r__,
vector<int>& params_i__) {

var lp__(0.0);
// model parameters
stan::io::reader<var> in__(params_r__,params_i__);

var sigma = in__.scalar_lb_constrain(0,lp__);

// transformed parameters
var sigma_sq;


// model body
{
var z;
}

return lp__;

} // log_prob()


void write_csv_header(std::ostream& o__) {
stan::io::csv_writer writer__(o__);
writer__.comma();
o__ << "sigma";
writer__.comma();
o__ << "sigma_sq";
writer__.comma();
o__ << "w";
writer__.newline();
}

void write_csv(std::vector<double>& params_r__,
std::vector<int>& params_i__,
std::ostream& o__) {
stan::io::reader<double> in__(params_r__,params_i__);
stan::io::csv_writer writer__(o__);
// read-transform, write parameters
double sigma = in__.scalar_lb_constrain(0);
writer__.write(sigma);

// declare and define transformed parameters
double sigma_sq;


// validate transformed parameters
assert(stan::prob::lb_validate(sigma_sq,0));

// write transformed parameters
writer__.write(sigma_sq);

// declare and define generated quantities
double w;


// validate generated quantities
assert(stan::prob::lb_validate(w,0));
assert(stan::prob::ub_validate(w, 1));

// write generated quantities
writer__.write(w);

writer__.newline();
}

}; // model

} // namespace

int main(int argc, const char* argv[]) {
try {

stan::gm::nuts_command<demo_model_namespace::demo_model>(argc,argv);
} catch (std::exception& e) {
std::cerr << std::endl << "Exception: " << e.what() << std::endl;
std::cerr << "Diagnostic information: " << std::endl <<
boost::diagnostic_information(e) << std::endl;
return -1;
}
}
